reasons: The canonical Sparkle corpus, re-run at the exact candidate SHA, reproduces its 2 regressions (>1) and fails the frozen bar.
The conservative pool over both binary-disjoint holdouts has 3 regressions over 110 distinct answerable cases, so the bar is not met in aggregate either.
Every regression replaces an already-correct Hex top-1 with an incorrect Jev choice, i.e. an exact-quality loss on that case.

Jev's own preference/confidence does not separate regressions from rescues (XA40 regressed at 0.33/0.32 and was rescued at 0.29/0.27), so any acceptance threshold would be an unprincipled bar; the goal forbids repairing ranking defects with thresholds or treating the score as a probability.
The regression count is not run-stable (1 then 0 on an identical repeat), so a single passing run is not proof of safety.
A genuine fix would have to change Hex's own candidate ordering or verdict strength, which is outside Jev integration scope, and the 2026-09-24 settlement ends further router generations.
